title: What is the future of work?
reason: 昨天的课程讨论通胀、供应与消费，今天轮换到工作方式和技术变化。本集比较关于 AI、远程办公和缩短工作周的预测，重点分析预测记录、岗位替代以及新旧岗位出现时间不一致的风险，适合联系平台建设、团队规划和职业发展。练习围绕六个常用表达重复调用，从原文支撑的填空逐步过渡到技术项目中的有限迁移。

targetExpressions.expression: take something with a pinch of salt
targetExpressions.meaning: not completely believe a claim because it may be inaccurate or unlikely
targetExpressions.usage: Use it for a doubtful claim: We should take confident technology forecasts with a pinch of salt.

targetExpressions.meaning: the achievements and failures shown by past performance
targetExpressions.usage: Use it when evaluating previous results: The supplier has a strong track record of reliable delivery.

targetExpressions.meaning: happen or become true, especially after being predicted
targetExpressions.usage: Use it for an expected event that eventually happens: The predicted reduction in workload never came to pass.

targetExpressions.meaning: be in danger of being harmed, lost or negatively affected
targetExpressions.usage: Use it to identify possible harm: Manual roles may be at risk when a process is automated.

targetExpressions.meaning: remove something that is no longer wanted or needed
targetExpressions.usage: Use it for deliberate removal: The upgrade lets us get rid of several manual steps.
Use it for an unplanned event or need: New compatibility issues can crop up during migration.

objectiveQuestions.explanation: The presenter asks whether current predictions should be taken with a pinch of salt because many earlier forecasts were inaccurate.

objectiveQuestions.prompt: What does a prediction expert's “track record” describe?

options.text: The number of hours they work each day
A list of future jobs they personally prefer
A route used by machines in a factory

objectiveQuestions.explanation: The transcript defines a track record as all the achievements or failures in someone's past performance.

objectiveQuestions.prompt: Complete Professor Burchell's point: Predictions of very large reductions in working time have not ______.
objectiveQuestions.explanation: He says dramatic historical predictions about reduced working time have not come to pass, meaning they have not happened.

objectiveQuestions.prompt: Complete Andrew Palmer's concern: Some jobs and professions ______ because of disruption from AI.
objectiveQuestions.explanation: Andrew expects some disruption from AI and explicitly says that certain jobs and professions are at risk.

objectiveQuestions.prompt: What does “get rid of all jobs” mean in the discussion?

options.text: Make every job more highly paid
Move all jobs into one office
Predict which jobs workers will enjoy

objectiveQuestions.explanation: Get rid of means remove something because it is no longer wanted; Andrew does not believe machines will eliminate every job.

objectiveQuestions.prompt: Complete the expectation: Economists say that new jobs will ______ after technology changes work.
objectiveQuestions.explanation: The transcript says new jobs will crop up, meaning they will appear unexpectedly.

objectiveQuestions.prompt: Why does Andrew Palmer worry about a sequencing risk?

options.text: Existing jobs may disappear before new jobs appear in a coordinated way.
Every new job will appear before any old job changes.
Economists can accurately schedule every future profession.
A four-day week always removes the need for worker support.

objectiveQuestions.explanation: He expects both disruption and new jobs, but worries they will not be aligned in time, leaving affected workers needing support.

objectiveQuestions.prompt: Which sentence uses “track record” naturally in a project decision?

options.text: We reviewed the vendor's track record before choosing its platform.
We track recorded the platform before choosing it.
The project ran a track record into production.
The vendor was track record by the team.

objectiveQuestions.explanation: A vendor's track record is its history of successes and failures, which is relevant evidence for a selection decision.

assessment.retellingPrompt: Without looking at the full transcript, retell the episode in 80–120 words using this structure: (1) topic—why predictions about work are difficult; (2) evidence—past predictions and possible AI disruption; (3) conclusion—why workers may need support when new jobs appear. Phrase bank: “take something with a pinch of salt”, “track record”, “crop up”. Use at least two phrases naturally. Simple, accurate sentences are enough.
referencePoints: Predictions about work have included robots taking over jobs, universal home working and much shorter working time.
Many dramatic predictions about reductions in working time have not come to pass, giving forecasters a weak track record.
Predictions should therefore be taken with a pinch of salt rather than accepted automatically.
Andrew Palmer does not think machines or AI will get rid of all jobs, but he expects some disruption.
Some jobs and professions are at risk, so affected workers may require support.
New jobs may crop up, but they may not appear at the same time as old jobs disappear, creating a sequencing risk.
